stem: The strength of interaction between particles determines whether the substance is a solid, liquid or gas at room temperature.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Lithium sulfide, $\text{Li}_2\text{S}$, is a crystalline solid with a melting point of $938^{\circ}\text{C}$. It conducts electricity when it is molten.
parts.text: Give the formulae of the particles present in solid lithium sulfide.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of the structure of the crystalline solid, why lithium sulfide has a high melting point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, is a gas at room temperature and pressure. It contains a coordinate bond.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by *coordinate bond*.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram to show the arrangement of outer electrons in $\text{CO}$.

Show the electrons belonging to the $\text{C}$ atom as $\times$.

Show the electrons belonging to the $\text{O}$ atom as $\bullet$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, is also a gas at room temperature and pressure. Neither $\text{CO}$ nor $\text{N}_2$ is an ideal gas.
parts.text: State two assumptions that are made about the behaviour of particles in an ideal gas.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{N}_2$ does not behave as an ideal gas at very high pressures.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete the table by naming **all** the types of intermolecular forces (van der Waals') in separate samples of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{CO(g)}$.

|  | $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ | $\text{CO(g)}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| number of electrons per molecule | $14$ | $14$ |
| presence of a dipole moment | $\times$ | $\checkmark$ |
| boiling point/$^{\circ}\text{C}$ | $-195.8$ | $-191.5$ |
| intermolecular forces (van der Waals') |  |  |

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest why the bond in a molecule of $\text{CO}$ contains a dipole moment.
